commitResults.messageBody: Package the shared split-view diff workflow inside the project so future Codex sessions can generate a self-contained HTML review of repository changes. Include the skill instructions, invocation metadata, and standard-library generator to keep the workflow reproducible for all project contributors.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for marking tasks as done
commitResults.messageBody: Track completion separately from task descriptions so list output can show each task's current status without introducing new classes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for unmarking completed tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Reuse the existing completion state so users can reverse a task's done status without adding new classes.
Define a reusable test-ui skill and runner, and require agents to review the UI test plan and execute it after code changes so user-visible behavior is checked consistently.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use an enum for chatbot command types
commitResults.messageBody: Centralize command keywords in CommandType and route input through an exhaustive switch so command handling no longer depends on repeated free-form strings. Preserve exact matching for no-argument commands and add regression coverage for unexpected list and bye arguments.

Save the complete task list after every successful mutation and reload it when Snoopy starts. Use a portable relative path, create missing directories, restore task types and completion states, and report unreadable or corrupted data without crashing.

Run each transcript in an isolated data directory and support restart and initial-file fixtures. Cover saving every mutation, loading all task types and statuses, first-run behavior, and graceful recovery from corrupted data.
Integrate automatic task saving and startup loading, including portable file handling, corrupted-data recovery, and restart-focused UI coverage.

Store deadline and event dates as LocalDate values, accept strict ISO input, and present dates in a readable English format. Preserve ISO dates in storage and reject invalid command or saved-file dates without mutating application state.
Update dated-task transcripts to use ISO input and formatted output. Add state-sensitive coverage for malformed and impossible dates, persisted dates across restart, and corrupted saved date records.
Integrate LocalDate parsing, readable date formatting, persisted date validation, and comprehensive date-focused UI coverage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Package Snoopy as an executable JAR
commitResults.messageBody: Point the application manifest at Snoopy so the Shadow JAR starts correctly. Add isolated storage construction and regression tests to verify command parsing, task behavior, and persistence before distribution.
Record the 50% high-value method target and require the test suite to stay current after code changes.

Group command, exception, storage, and task types by responsibility while keeping src/main/java as the source root. Update tests, launcher configuration, and documentation for the new qualified class names.

The production code has inconsistent switch indentation, broad field visibility, and Javadoc tags without punctuation. These issues make the code harder to read and diverge from the required course standard.\n\nAlign switch cases, narrow task fields, and standardize Javadoc tags so the code follows the SE-EDU basic and intermediate conventions without changing behavior.

Users cannot locate a task without reading the complete list. This becomes inconvenient as the task list grows.\n\nAdd a find command that searches task descriptions for a case-sensitive substring and displays matching tasks without changing stored state. Cover command parsing, matching semantics, empty input, and state preservation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Limit command variables to case scope
commitResults.messageBody:
The command switch shares one scope across traditional case labels.
This forces later branches to reuse variables declared by earlier branches
and violates the coding standard's smallest-scope rule.

Use arrow-style switch branches so each command owns its variables while
preserving the existing command behavior.

Future Java changes need a reusable summary of the project's required
basic and intermediate coding rules.

Add a project-specific skill covering naming, layout, declarations, and
Javadoc so later code changes can apply the same standard consistently.

Future commits need consistent subjects and informative bodies that follow
the course conventions.

Add a project-specific skill that captures the required subject format,
body structure, and review checks for cohesive commits.

The project skills are available but agents are not yet required to use
them during Java edits or commit preparation.

Require both skills in AGENTS.md so future work follows the same Java and
Git standards by default.
